definition: A practicum is a supervised training phase in which trainees apply what they have learned in real-world settings. In this psychology-related teaching context, it refers to pre-service teachers working in actual classrooms and dealing with practical and emotional demands.

reasons: The packet supports practicum as a phase in teacher education with real classroom challenges, but it does not support the added claim that it is a supervised training phase.

The definition adds “practical and emotional demands” in a generalized way; the packet specifically mentions emotionally demanding practicum contexts, but not as a general dictionary sense of the term.
The field label “cognition” is not supported by the packet, which is about teacher education/practicum rather than a cognition term.
The packet discusses “teaching practicum” as a phase where pre-service teachers encounter real classroom challenges, but it does not explicitly define practicum as a “supervised training phase.”

The definition’s phrase “in real-world settings” is broadly consistent with “real classroom challenges,” but the packet does not clearly support the exact wording/scope as a general definitional feature (e.g., “real-world settings” as part of the term’s definition).

The part about “practical and emotional demands” is only partially supported: the packet mentions “emotionally demanding practicum contexts” and psychological readiness, but it does not explicitly define practicum as involving “practical and emotional demands” in those exact terms.
